stories.s: Fighting has returned to northern Ethiopia, shattering a fragile peace in the region. DW spoke to civilians caught in the crossfire amid communication blackouts, as rebel and federal forces keep battling for territory.

stories.t: Son of Zambian bishop detained in post-election raid fears for his father's safety
stories.s: Trevor Mwamba was detained last month with other opposition figures and charged with treason, his son says.

stories.t: Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack
stories.s: The suspect, 24, was arrested before the alleged cyber attack took place.

stories.t: Nigerian dances non-stop for seven days in world record bid
stories.s: Crowds cheered on Ben Dancer as completed his challenge and he has now gone to hospital for a check-up

stories.t: Close-up look at Turner's '£50m' Rome painting on show in the city
stories.s: Turner’s early 19th century painting - Rome, from Mount Aventine - will be on display in the Italian capital for the first time ahead of an auction in London in December.

stories.t: US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy takes effect as trade war drags on
stories.s: It is the latest escalation in the Canada-US trade war after negotiations collapsed in late August, with no word on when talks may resume.

stories.t: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
stories.s: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

stories.t: North Korea has recently completed two road bridges easing transport to strategic allies Russia and China
stories.s: Two recently opened bridges are expected to ease trade and transport between North Korea and its powerful neighbors. The new connections come as Pyongyang builds strategic ties with China and Russia.

stories.t: Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar
stories.s: Human rights groups say some 5,000 returnees could face violence, persecution and forced conscription.

stories.t: Women and children displaced by Nepal's floods say safe housing, privacy and stability remain out of reach
stories.s: Families living in temporary shelters in northern Nepal say safety and privacy remain out of reach as concerns about trafficking and abuse mount.

stories.t: 'I was lured into a trap': Evan Gershkovich on moment that led to 16 months in Russian jail
stories.s: The US journalist says he realised he was a "a pawn in a greater game" when he was not interrogated or tortured by FSB agents.

stories.t: Israeli settlers attack West Bank village and block Palestinian family's return home
stories.s: Two homes belonging to the al-Tubasi family were set on fire and Israeli security forces were also targeted by settlers.

stories.t: French hard-right leader accuses opponents of 'total war' after claims of antisemitism
stories.s: National Rally President Jordan Bardella says he will sue for libel over comments he is accused of making as a young activist.

stories.t: Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
stories.s: The storm moved ashore on the Baja California peninsula, which is a popular tourist destination.

stories.t: Celine Dion kicks off Paris Fashion Week with surprise performance
stories.s: The singer appeared at the end of L'Oreal's annual show as the French fashion bonanza kicked off.

stories.t: Watch: Luxury units uncovered inside an Indonesian prison
stories.s: A surprise inspection at the prison revealed apartment-like units appearing to house inmates, equipped with televisions, a gym and fridges stocked with alcohol.

stories.t: As the U.S. signals a smaller Middle East footprint, Turkey is ready to step in
stories.s: Turkey's bid for regional influence comes as the Middle East has been hit by profound shocks that started with the Hamas-led 2023 attack on Israel and continue with the seven-month-old war on Iran.

stories.t: How an alleged rape sent an Indian university into turmoil and emptied hostels
stories.s: Police are trying to verify whether a female student was raped at Lovely Professional University (LPU).

stories.t: Burkina Faso's junta leader opens major gold refinery to keep mining profits at home
stories.s: Junta leader Ibrahim Traoré wants the country to profit more from its mineral wealth.

stories.t: From Jamui to Delhi, the burden of safety from sexual assault cannot fall on women
stories.s: As outrage grows over cases​ of sexual violence, activists are demanding a shift from controlling women to confronting men’s behaviour. Plus, Tony Klor’s ‘hella dope’ city vlogs • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up…

stories.t: Watch: Bangkok locals create floating market during floods
stories.s: As sellers waded through floodwaters to sell produce like fish and vegetables from floating platforms and foam boxes, buyers walked or paddled between the makeshift stalls to buy their groceries.

stories.t: Rights group accuses Vietnam of abducting Australian and Norwegian activists
stories.s: Vietnam says the men entered the country illegally and accused them of planning terrorist activities.

stories.t: Czech Republic ready for Wembley 30 years after Euro '96
stories.s: The Czech Republic are returning to Wembley for a Nations League game with England, just over 30 years after their Euro '96 heartbreak there.
